response.name: 403 Permission denied

request.description: A company-scoped caller is always forced into their own company, regardless of any companyId sent — creates a custom role private to that company. A platform admin may omit companyId for a global role, or supply one to create it on behalf of a specific company. permissionIds must reference real Permission ids, not role ids — the placeholder above is illustrative only; substitute a real permission id. Two different companies may each have a role with the same name.

response.name: 201 Created
403 Permission denied
404 Permission not found
409 Global role name already exists

request.description: Platform admin can update any non-system role; a company-scoped caller only their own company's custom roles (403 ROLE_ACCESS_DENIED for a global role or another company's role). System roles (Company Admin/Company Member) can never be updated by anyone (403 SYSTEM_ROLE_PROTECTED). permissionIds, if provided, REPLACES the full permission set.

response.name: 200 OK
403 No access to this role
403 System role protected
404 Not found

request.description: Same ownership/system-role rules as Update a role. Also blocked with 409 ROLE_IN_USE if any user currently holds this role.

response.name: 403 System role protected
409 Role in use

request.description: A company-scoped caller (e.g. the owner from Auth > Register) is always forced into their own company — the companyId above is ignored/overridden if it doesn't match. A platform admin can use companyId to target any company, or omit it to create another company-less admin. Accepts an optional roleIds array (see Roles > List roles for IDs) — a company-scoped caller creating a teammate without specifying roleIds defaults to the Company Member role, so nobody is ever role-less.
